entries.body:
## Context

`align-workspace-with-current-capacities` is already archived with its implementation tasks complete, but the current `dev` Quality workflow fails while re-validating its lifecycle boundary test.

`tests/object-lifecycle-contracts.test.mjs` intentionally checks the historical finishing diff (`0898ca1^..bb32265`). GitHub Actions checks out `dev` with the default shallow history (`fetch-depth: 1`), so those revisions are unavailable and the otherwise-green test suite fails.

## Change

- configure `actions/checkout@v6` with `fetch-depth: 0`
- preserve the historical ownership assertion instead of weakening/removing the test
- no product behavior, storage schema, editor ownership, or OpenSpec contract changes

## Verification target

- `pnpm verify`
- Quality CI should proceed past the historical lifecycle test and continue through coverage/build

entries.title: docs: define agent loop engineering
entries.body:
### Summary

- Added a minimal main-agent loop contract to `AGENTS.md`.
- Clarified software verification vs OpenSpec verification and failure diagnosis in `docs/TESTING.md`.
- Refreshed the existing `architect`, `test-engineer`, `code-reviewer`, and `security-reviewer` subagents with current repo facts and supported Antigravity tool names.
- Added OpenSpec change `improve-agent-loop-engineering` for the durable loop-engineering contract.

### Why

The audit found the repository already has a strong harness, so the right fix was not a new orchestrator or framework. The concrete gaps were stale subagent facts, unsupported Antigravity-style tool declarations, missing bounded retry/no-progress guidance, missing explicit DONE/BLOCKED/ESCALATE states, and unclear separation between software verification and OpenSpec verification.

### OpenSpec

Created `openspec/changes/improve-agent-loop-engineering` with new capability `agent-loop-engineering`.

Acceptance covered:

- main agent controls the execution loop;
- OpenSpec remains the durable requirements authority;
- software verification is distinct from OpenSpec verification;
- subagent delegation is focused and shallow;
- subagent definitions match supported runtime tools;
- verification failures trigger diagnosis;
- retries are bounded and no-progress is detected;
- terminal states are explicit;
- high-impact actions remain human-gated;
- review rigor is proportional to risk.

### Verification

Executed successfully:

- `openspec.cmd validate improve-agent-loop-engineering`
- `openspec.cmd status --change improve-agent-loop-engineering`
- `openspec.cmd validate --changes`
- `npx.cmd -y pnpm@11.20.0 verify`
- `git diff --check`
- `git diff --cached --check`

`pnpm verify` passed Biome, Next.js type generation, TypeScript, Vitest, and Next.js production build.

### Subagent validation

- Checked current official Antigravity docs for custom subagent discovery and supported tool names.
- Static validation confirmed no legacy `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, or `Bash` tool declarations remain.
- Tool lists now use `view_file`, `grep_search`, `find_by_name`, and `run_command` only where command verification is useful.
- Direct Antigravity runtime invocation from this PowerShell session was blocked because `ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS` is not set.
- Independent code-reviewer subagent reviewed the diff and reported no actionable findings.

### Deferred intentionally

- New orchestrator agent or multi-agent framework.
- Custom loop state, memory files, hooks, telemetry, or eval platform.
- Parallel write/worktree automation.
- New MCP servers, skills, dependencies, or CI jobs.
- Archiving OpenSpec changes before CI/review completion.

entries.title: test: add verification harness
entries.body:
## Summary

- Added a canonical `pnpm verify` command covering lint, Next.js type generation, TypeScript, Vitest, and production build.
- Added Vitest + React Testing Library with one real component test for the current notes workspace page.
- Updated CI to run `pnpm verify` while preserving the required `Quality` check name.
- Documented Definition of Done and E2E trigger points in existing canonical docs.
- Added an OpenSpec change for the verification harness contract.
- Added `.gitattributes` so formatting checks are deterministic across Windows/Linux line endings.

## Why

The audit showed the repository already has substantial context, Git workflow docs, agent rules, specialized agents, skills, OpenSpec workflows, and protected-branch CI. The highest-value gap was objective verification: no test runner, no canonical local health command, and CI/local checks were manually duplicated.

This keeps the harness small: one command, one focused test setup, one spec-driven contract, and no new agents, MCPs, hooks, or duplicate harness documents.

## OpenSpec

Created `openspec/changes/add-verification-harness`.

Relevant requirements:

- canonical local verification command;
- CI uses the canonical verification while preserving `Quality`;
- automated component testing for current UI behavior;
- risk-proportional evidence for Definition of Done;
- E2E deferred until critical flows justify it;
- cross-platform text normalization.

## Verification

Executed successfully:

- `npx.cmd -y pnpm@11.20.0 install --frozen-lockfile`
- `npx.cmd -y pnpm@11.20.0 verify`
- `git diff --check`
- `git diff --cached --check`
- `openspec.cmd validate add-verification-harness`
- `openspec.cmd status --change add-verification-harness`

`pnpm verify` passed Biome, Next.js type generation, TypeScript, Vitest, and Next.js production build. Vitest reported 1 test file passed and 1 test passed.

## Deferred intentionally

- Playwright E2E: useful later when auth, persistence, note mutation, or deployment smoke flows exist.
- Harness eval platform: premature until repeatable comparable agent tasks exist.
- New MCPs or skills: not justified by the audit.
- Hooks: CI and package scripts solve the current need with less agent-specific coupling.
- Architecture linting: premature for the current small app boundaries.
- Runtime or agent observability platform: premature for current complexity.
